title: How data is asked for
headline: All 14 verified findings stand, none argues from a feature being unused, and each now has ordered steps, the tests and rules that hold it, and one check; two were added. Today's cost is small (the listed app statements total about 39 minutes of database time in 78 days) because production holds only the team's demo stores, so what counts before opening is shape: one read fetches every published page whole to find one page (79,778 calls, 781 s), 122 store filters are written so the store index cannot serve them, the five-minute dispatcher starts 78 jobs on 5 connections, and 91,200 of 216,877 transactions deleted nothing. The two additions grow with orders and catalogue size: five document jobs find their due work each tick by re-checking every store's orders of 120 days and every invoice ever issued, and the catalogue listing calls a VAT function per product row (11.3 µs a row measured, against 0.1 µs when each rate is asked once). Do first: the statement counter (DQ-11), the store filter (DQ-8), the slug lookup (DQ-9), the knowledge job (DQ-6), the AI month sum (DQ-4) and the page index (DQ-2).

clean: No finding in this dimension rests on a feature being unused; where the first auditor argued from an empty table the verified report kept only the running cost, and so does this plan.

src/db/client.ts: one pool per instance (max 5, idle 5 s) attached to Vercel's lifecycle, node-postgres chosen for the transaction pooler with the reason written down (D37), no named prepared statements anywhere.
Statement and lock limits are the role's (15 s, 5 s) and a longer one is taken with set local inside a transaction (longerTimeout, client.ts:89-92), never a plain set through the pooler.
Transactions around single reads are rare: 12 read-only by their text among the 296 the scan could parse, each with a reason.
Counting by loading rows is rare (6 heuristic hits in 1,648 selects), and offset paging is rare (11 uses in 10 files, all admin lists and version lists).
The read replica (replicaDb, client.ts:105-110) is built but off, used by one module (analytics-totals.ts), and costs nothing while READ_DATABASE_URL is unset.
publishedPageNames (pages.ts:713-735) pulls titles out of the JSON in SQL instead of fetching documents: the right shape, and the model for DQ-2.

Queues are claimed with for update skip locked (integrations.ts:1033-1039, cookie-scans.ts:78-83), and store events are a real queue with done marks (staff-alerts.ts processStoreEvents), so the minute route's alert work follows what waits.

The dispatcher's prune deletes are served by an index on their time column (search_queries_created_idx, search_cache_created_idx, recommendation_events_created_idx, recommendation_adds_created_idx, form_submissions_created_idx, api_idempotency_keys_created_idx, docs_reads_day_idx, oauth_tokens_expires_idx): they will not scan the growing tables. Their cadence is DQ-5's matter.

A page view is recorded with two statements (one read, one upsert that also counts product views) plus a rate check for a new visitor (analytics-visits.ts recordVisit): lean for the write that will grow fastest.
cronAuthorised() reads the scheduler's secret from Vault at most every five minutes per instance (cron-auth.ts:18-31), not on every call.

Several dispatcher jobs already ask only for stores where the feature is set up (staff-alerts.ts joins staff_alert_settings; order-archive.ts starts from order_settings.auto_archive_days). The chat agent is off by default, so the knowledge job's cost follows the stores that switch it on.
bonus_expire_due and the VAT-label midnight check are one set-based statement a tick each (2.1 ms and 7.3 ms a call): the right shape for a job over all stores.
getStore() reads one wide row per store and is cached per store (stores.ts:231-277): one statement in place of many small ones.
The admin's session, account and membership reads are wrapped in React cache() (auth.ts:121, 215, 354, 407), and cart, checkout and order share one read per request through perRequest().
status_checks is pruned at 91 days (status.ts:265); the statistics file's note 'never pruned' is wrong.
The proxy's two store reads are kept 10 s per instance (redirect-resolve.ts:203-232, house-switch.ts:31-43): single-row reads whose cost follows shopper traffic.
media.url has a unique index and thumbnail_url an index (baseline_3_rules.sql:2884, 9796), so alt-text lookups can use them once the table is large.

findings.title: Nine routes are called every minute whether or not there is work, and one of their questions grows with the number of stores
findings.evidence: pg_cron schedules nine jobs with '* * * * *' (baseline_4:93-103; I counted 9), each a net.http_post that also reads the cron secret from Vault. Production: 352,514 calls, 3,974 s, 11.3 ms each. Each run polls without first asking whether anything waits. Cookie scan: two updates, then a CTE over every open site with two correlated subqueries on cookie_scans written 'is not distinct from' (cookie-scans.ts:94-99); the table's only fitting index is (store_id, created_at) (baseline_3:7591) and that wording cannot use it, so production shows 1,101,927 sequential scans of cookie_scans over 49,338 calls: 22 scans a call, 873 rows a scan. Theme shots: every run calls queueThemeShots() first (theme-shots.ts:331), which reads every published theme with its whole snapshot, the theme contents, the showcase stores and the stored queue, then opens a transaction with an advisory lock to claim; production shows 35,101 such theme reads (101 s) against a theme_shots table of 72 rows, although three callers already queue shots when a theme or demo store changes (askForThemeShots: store-starters.ts:326, design-presets.ts:825 and 2368) and a partial index on the waiting units exists (theme_shots_queue_idx, baseline_3:14031). Pack pictures opens a lock transaction each minute (content-packs.ts:735-737). Together the two lock claims are the 71,422 pg_advisory_xact_lock calls. The integrations route runs seven pollers a minute (inbound email, workflows, the platform's workflows, deliveries, the platform's deliveries, support emails, store events) and deliverDue() ends every run with a prune delete (integrations.ts:1062; 66,533 calls each of the claim and the delete). The autopilot's three runners each read the pause switch (ai-pause.ts:18; 69,075 calls). Eight of the nine routes answer first and work in after(), so the ledger's 0 to 1 ms durations do not show idleness; the row counts do.
findings.cost: 12,960 function calls a day by the schedule, fixed whatever the store count. At most about 150 s of database time a day for the calls themselves (13,248 calls at 11.3 ms). What grows: the cookie scan's who-is-due query does 2 table scans per open site per minute; estimate, at 1,000 open stores that is 2,000 scans a minute of a table of about 13,000 rows. The theme-shot polling grows with themes, not stores.
findings.who_pays: The database and the server (function invocations), every minute. No shopper or owner waits for it.
fix_steps: 1 (S, first). Cookie scan's due query, src/server/cookie-scans.ts:85-110: write the 'last' CTE so an index serves it. For stores: from sites s left join lateral (select max(c.finished_at) filter (where c.status = 'done') as done_at, max(c.created_at) as tried_at from commerce.cookie_scans c where c.store_id = s.store_id) l on true. For the platform's row: the same subquery with c.store_id is null. Combine the two with union all. Keep the insert, the order and the on conflict clause as they are.

2. No new index is needed. My EXPLAIN of the rewritten query on the local scratch database (read-only, enable_seqscan off) shows both branches as an Index Cond on the existing cookie_scans_store_created_idx (store_id = the site, and store_id is null for the platform); one site holds about 13 rows (a weekly scan kept 90 days). In src/server/site-cookies.ts:44-47 write the store filter with the owned() helper of DQ-8 so the banner's read of the latest finished scan is served the same way (my EXPLAIN: Index Cond on store_id, then a sort of that site's few rows).

3. Weekly scans from an hourly pass. Split claimScan(): keep, every minute, the stale-running update and the claim of a queued scan (my EXPLAIN: both go through the partial index cookie_scans_one_active_idx, which holds only waiting and running scans). Move the due query into a new queueDueScans(limit = 20) in the same file that inserts due sites as status 'queued' with requested_by null. Call it from the dispatcher as a job with an hourly cadence once DQ-5 gives jobs cadences; until then call it from src/app/api/cron/cookie-scan/route.ts only when new Date().getUTCMinutes() === 0 (the pattern autopilot-effects.ts:44 uses). One scan a minute still gives room for 10,000 weekly scans.

4. Theme shots, src/app/api/cron/theme-shots/route.ts:21-32 and src/server/theme-shots.ts:330-342: before after(), ask one statement, select exists (select 1 from commerce.theme_shots where status in ('waiting', 'running')), which my EXPLAIN shows as an index-only scan of theme_shots_queue_idx; when false answer { started: false } and do nothing else. In runThemeShots() stop calling queueThemeShots() on every run: work out wantedNow() only after the first unit is claimed (takeThemeShot needs it). Bring the queue in line where it changes: the three askForThemeShots() callers stay, and add one daily sweep (queueThemeShots() then pruneThemeShots()) as a dispatcher job claimed with claimDay('daily.theme-shot-sweep', …) as ui-nightly.ts:73 does.

5. Pack pictures, src/server/content-packs.ts:733-750 claimPack(): before opening the lock transaction ask select exists (select 1 from commerce.store_starters where pictures_wanted_at is not null) and return null when false.

6. Prunes out of the minute: remove the delete at src/server/integrations.ts:1062 from deliverDue() and its twin in src/server/platform-integrations.ts deliverPlatformDue(); export them as pruneDeliveries() and prunePlatformDeliveries() (platform-integrations.ts:484) and run both from the dispatcher with a daily cadence (DQ-5), or from runRetention().

7. Autopilot route, src/app/api/cron/autopilot/route.ts:19-30: read aiAutonomyPaused() once in the route and pass the answer to the three runners, which today each call skipWhilePaused() (autopilot-runner.ts:58, autopilot-reviews.ts:114, autopilot-events.ts:179).

8 (optional, last, only if function invocations show on the bill). Put the due test in the scheduler's own SQL so no HTTP call is made when a queue is empty. It keeps each route's due test in two places (a migration and the code) and needs a heartbeat so the ledger does not read the route as late. Not recommended before opening: once real stores exist the queues have work most minutes and the saving shrinks.

findings.evidence: listPublishedPages() (pages.ts:664-681) selects id, slug, published (the whole document) and two dates for every published page of an owner, parses each with zod, then looks up library alt texts for every picture on every page (withPageAlts). I listed its call sites with rg: 35. At least 12 then do .find() for one id: the front page (s/[store]/[market]/page.tsx:29), the products page (pages.ts:799), a page by id (pages.ts:862), the platform's role pages (platform-roles.ts:37), the checkout's terms (checkout-terms.ts:46), three account pages, the blog's listing page (blog-listing.tsx:89), the chat's page (site-chat.tsx:110) and two admin previews. Others read only titles: the platform's header and footer load every page and every article whole to build a map of id, slug and title (platform-navigation.ts:138-146); a store's footer loads them all to print up to five legal titles (legal-links.ts:24-29); generateStaticParams loads them all for the slugs (s/[store]/[market]/[slug]/page.tsx:20). findings.title: "Where is this picture used" scans every page's text for each picture, and the job re-checks every picture daily
findings.evidence: mediaUses() joins each picture to every page of the site and tests position(m.url in pg.draft::text) and the same on published, so both documents of every page are cast to text per picture; it does the same over entries, menus, saved parts, theme looks and settings in 12 union branches (media-library.ts:321-381). Production: 1,831 calls at 145 ms, and other shapes 43 at 925 ms, 198 at 133 ms, 205 at 66 ms, 776 at 47 ms: about 382 s in all, the second most expensive app statement. embedMedia() (media-library.ts:798-831, which I opened) picks every picture whose vector is older than a day ('or e.updated_at < now() - interval ''1 day''', line 810, 'so what uses an item is kept current'), 128 a run, calls mediaUses() for them, then only moves the date on the unchanged ones (822-828): media_embeddings shows 13,414 updates on 468 rows, about 29 daily re-stamps of each. refreshMediaEmbeddings() loops over every site with media, one after another (860-874), every five minutes.
findings.cost: About 382 s in 78 days on 699 pictures. It grows with pictures times pages times page size per store, every day, for every store with media and an AI connection, whether or not anything changed. Estimate: a store with 2,000 pictures and 100 pages of 50 KB scans about 20 GB of text a day.
findings.who_pays: The database, daily per picture, driven by the five-minute dispatcher; an owner opening the media library (two calls per page of the library).
fix_steps: 1 (S, first). In src/server/media-library.ts embedMedia(): replace the daily clause at line 810 with a change test. Once per site per run read one stamp, the latest change of anything that can hold a picture: greatest of max(updated_at) over the site's rows in the tables the 12 branches of mediaUses() read (lines 321-381: pages, product media and products, content entries, menus, saved parts, theme looks, settings). Pass it into the stale query as 'or e.updated_at < the stamp'. A site where nothing changed since its vectors were stamped then returns no stale rows and mediaUses() is not called. A table without an updated_at column keeps the daily clause for its branch only; say which in a comment.

findings.title: Five document jobs find their due work by re-checking every store's recent orders, invoices and refunds on each tick
findings.evidence: Not in the verified report, which names only the invoice job's repeated per-store calls. invoiceJobs() runs every five minutes from the dispatcher. Its store finder (invoice-issue.ts:71-101) has no queue: it takes every order of every store placed in the last 120 days and proves for each that an invoice exists (an anti-join on invoices and a look in order_events), then every succeeded refund ever made (no time bound) against credit_notes and order_events, then every outside-refunded return. Invoicing is on unless switched off (coalesce(cfg.enabled, true), line 76), so every selling store's orders are in. My EXPLAIN on the local scratch database (PostgreSQL 16.15, read-only, enable_seqscan off): orders is entered through orders_invoice_candidates_idx, which is (store_id, placed_at), with placed_at as the only condition, so the whole index is walked; refunds through refunds_store_id_key with status as a Filter, so every refund is read. For each store found the job calls issue_waiting_invoices(), which itself ends with issue_missing_credit_notes() (baseline_1:10554), and then calls issue_missing_credit_notes() again (invoice-issue.ts:125): twice per store per tick (production: 9,909 calls each, 132 s and 35 s). In the same tick sendPendingDocumentNotices() (invoice-notices.ts:130-170) reads every invoice and credit note issued in 3 days, each with a look in order_events, document_deliveries and email_messages; invoices and credit_notes have no index that starts with a time (invoices_issued_idx is (store_id, issued_on), baseline_3:9222; credit_notes_issued_idx the same, :7654), and my EXPLAIN shows a walk of invoices_store_id_key with issued_at as a Filter: every invoice ever issued, every five minutes. runEinvoiceSending() (einvoice-sending.ts:57-97) reads every invoice, credit note, work invoice and work credit note of 2 days and opens each one's snapshot JSON to see whether the buyer is a business (my EXPLAIN: the snapshot test is a Filter after a bitmap scan on issued_on); a consumer's invoice is never recorded as looked at, so it is read again on every tick for two days. collectSupplierOrders() (supplier-orders.ts:58-73) does the same over 3 days of stock movements, but only at suppliers' locations, so its cost follows the stores that drop-ship.
findings.cost: Nothing measurable today (102 orders in all). After opening the work per tick is in proportion to all stores' orders, not to what waits. Estimate: at 1,000 stores with 10 orders a day, 1.2 million orders are re-proved every five minutes (two index probes each), every invoice ever issued is filtered for the email check, and 20,000 invoice snapshots are opened for the e-invoice check. The role's statement limit is 15 s; a store finder that passes it fails the whole invoice job, and then waiting invoices are not issued.
findings.who_pays: The database, every five minutes, for every store that sells; later store owners and their customers, if the job times out and invoices wait.
fix_steps: 1. Indexes that fit the two short windows, in one custom migration (pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name document_job_indexes, then node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs; none of these tables is on the hot-table list, so plain create index): invoices (issued_at); credit_notes (issued_at); invoices (issued_on) where (snapshot -> 'buyer' ->> 'type') = 'business'; the same partial index on credit_notes; work_invoices (issued_on) where status <> 'draft' and not imported and (buyer ->> 'business')::boolean is true; work_credit_notes (issued_on) where (buyer ->> 'business')::boolean is true. The statements at invoice-notices.ts:131-139 and :140-162 and einvoice-sending.ts:64-93 already carry these predicates, so no code changes: the email check reads 3 days of documents and the e-invoice check reads only business documents and never opens a consumer's snapshot.

2. The invoice job's finder, src/server/invoice-issue.ts:71-101: keep today's query as the net and run it once an hour (DQ-5's cadence; until then the minute-below-5 test of autopilot-effects.ts:44). Add to its refunds branch rf.created_at > now() - make_interval(days => LOOKBACK_DAYS), which refunds_store_created_idx can then help with per store, and an order by store_id before the limit so no store is starved when more than 50 have work.

3. A fast path for every tick that reads only what is marked as waiting: stores with an order_events row of type 'invoice.failed' in the last 120 days whose order still has no invoice (add a partial index order_events (created_at) where type = 'invoice.failed'; the event is written at baseline_1:10517), plus stores with an applied order change whose documents wait (add a partial index order_edits (store_id) where status = 'applied' and documents = 'waiting').

4. A try at once where the cause goes away: where the seller's details or the invoice settings are saved (find the writers with rg 'invoice_settings' src/server), call issueWaitingInvoices(storeId) in after(), so an owner who completes the details does not wait for the hourly net.

5. One credit-note call per store: issue_waiting_invoices() already ends with issue_missing_credit_notes(). In invoiceJobs() (invoice-issue.ts:123-126) call issueMissingCreditNotes(storeId) only when issueWaitingInvoices() failed; make it return that fact instead of swallowing it into a 0.

6. Write the pattern down in docs/wave-1b-invoices.md (the job's section) and docs/rules/admin/commerce.md: a document job reads a waiting mark or a window an index can serve, and keeps the full check as an hourly net.

findings.title: The catalogue's listing reads call a VAT function and an alt-text function once per product row, and Postgres cannot fold them into the query
findings.evidence: Not in the verified report beyond one line on store_is_active(). listProducts() (catalog.ts:284-330) returns every active product of a store and market with no limit (code review step 3.9) and selects commerce.vat_rate(market, p.vat_category) (line 312) and commerce.media_alt(m.url, locale) (line 299) per row; listGridProducts() does the same (lines 676 and 689). Both are stable SQL functions with SET search_path (baseline_1:20704-20725 and 12341-12350), which Postgres does not inline, so each row runs the function's own query: vat_rate reads countries joined to vat_rates up to three times. My counts (rg, tests left out): vat_rate 48 uses in 33 files, media_alt 9 in 6, store_is_active 69 in 44; the local database has 91 stable SQL functions with a SET clause in commerce. Measured on the local scratch database (PostgreSQL 16.15, read-only, explain analyze): vat_rate over 10,000 product rows 112.9 ms, 11.3 µs a row; the same rows joined to a materialized list of the store's distinct VAT categories, each rate asked once, 0.9 ms; store_is_active over 10,002 rows 24.1 ms against 0.5 ms for the plain expression; media_alt 48.8 ms for 10,000 rows on an empty media table. Production agrees: countries (28 rows) is the second most sequentially scanned table, 375,215 scans reading 10.5 M rows, which is 28 rows a scan: whole-table reads of a table only this function family reads per row; my 10,000 local calls added 20,000 such scans.
findings.cost: About 11 µs per product row per catalogue read for the VAT rate, plus at least 5 µs per row for the alt text: 0.3 ms for a 20-product demo store; estimate 80 ms or more for a 5,000-product catalogue on each cold listing, grid, feed or sitemap read. Small today. It grows with one store's catalogue, and store_is_active() per row grows with all stores' rows in the jobs that call it over whole tables (embeddings.ts:31-45).
findings.who_pays: The database; the first visitor of a listing after its cache is cold.
fix_steps: 1. In src/server/catalog.ts add one sql fragment used by listProducts() and listGridProducts(): a CTE rates as materialized (select c.cat, commerce.vat_rate(market, c.cat) as rate from (select distinct vat_category as cat from commerce.products where store_id = the store) c). Join it (join rates r on r.cat = p.vat_category) and select r.rate as vat_rate in place of the per-row call at lines 312 and 689. The rate still comes from commerce.vat_rate(country, products.vat_category), as the rule in CLAUDE.md (Database) asks; nothing reads countries.standard_vat_rate.

2. The alt text in the same two reads: replace commerce.media_alt(m.url, locale) by a lateral left join on commerce.media with the function's own where, order and limit (baseline_1:12345-12349), and take image_width from the same join; today line 302 reads commerce.media a second time per row for the width.

3. store_is_active() in statements that return many rows: join commerce.stores and write the three conditions through one shared fragment (export const activeStore = (s) => sql`${s}.status = 'active' and not ${s}.starter and not ${s}.sandbox` in src/server/stores.ts; media-library.ts:862 writes them by hand today). Move embeddings.ts:31-45 (with DQ-5 step 3) and the list reads in staff-alerts.ts, support-email.ts and the autopilot runners. Leave single-row guards on the function.

4. Do not remove SET search_path from the functions to make them inlinable: src/db/vat.test.ts:771, fulfilment.test.ts:874 and notifications.test.ts:482 hold a fixed search_path on every function for the security advisor.
5. getProduct() (catalog.ts:371) reads one product: leave it.
